question: Is the composition 0.000 a no-viable-code generation failure or a wrong-program (semantic) failure, and does it survive length-matched and surface-matched controls?

controls.e_per_composite_decomposition: every condition x op reports syntax / valid / solve-defined / executable / pass@1 + parse|allowlist|zero_pass|partial|all_pass

design: matched controls around the exposure experiment: one model trained on primitives + exposed composites (identical to run_composition_exposure), seven conditions forming a structure x surface 2x2 at primitive-matched program length, with paired instances (ref code + hidden tests held fixed, only the prompt changes)
seeding_note: corrected-pipeline pattern: both random.seed and torch.manual_seed are set from --seed; the original run_composition_exposure.py seeded only torch, so its checkpoint was not bitwise-reproducible (Dataset.batch samples with global random)

tokenizer.corpus: train+exposed then heldout (exact exposure order); control texts rely on the complete byte alphabet

decode.early_stop: 16 consecutive NUL tokens (lossless for NUL-truncated extraction)

length_matching.note: token counts under the run tokenizer; new composites asserted inside the mastered-primitive range (control c)

primitive_unseen_surface.role: control (a): SEEN program structure, UNSEEN wording — reference code and hidden tests byte-identical to primitive_native

exposed_native.role: anchor: composites seen in training (pipeline upper bound)

heldout_native.role: baseline: the book's failing condition (unseen composite, native unseen family prompt)

heldout_seen_surface.role: control (b): UNSEEN composite structure under a VERBATIM training surface frame — ref code + tests identical to heldout_native

new_composite_unseen_surface.role: control (c): NEW length-matched composite, novel wording — 2x2 cell unseen structure x unseen surface

new_composite_seen_surface.role: control (c)+(b): NEW length-matched composite under a VERBATIM training frame — 2x2 cell unseen structure x seen surface

decomposition: no-viable-code vs wrong-program split per condition (favorable256 decode): primitive_native: 0/300 no-viable-code (syntax 1.000), 0/300 wrong-program (0 zero-pass + 0 partial), 300/300 pass (pass@1 1.000); primitive_unseen_surface: 299/300 no-viable-code (syntax 0.020), 1/300 wrong-program (1 zero-pass + 0 partial), 0/300 pass (pass@1 0.000); exposed_native: 0/120 no-viable-code (syntax 1.000), 40/120 wrong-program (40 zero-pass + 0 partial), 80/120 pass (pass@1 0.667); heldout_native: 120/120 no-viable-code (syntax 0.000), 0/120 wrong-program (0 zero-pass + 0 partial), 0/120 pass (pass@1 0.000); heldout_seen_surface: 112/120 no-viable-code (syntax 0.075), 8/120 wrong-program (8 zero-pass + 0 partial), 0/120 pass (pass@1 0.000); new_composite_unseen_surface: 80/80 no-viable-code (syntax 0.000), 0/80 wrong-program (0 zero-pass + 0 partial), 0/80 pass (pass@1 0.000); new_composite_seen_surface: 80/80 no-viable-code (syntax 0.000), 0/80 wrong-program (0 zero-pass + 0 partial), 0/80 pass (pass@1 0.000)
conclusion: **Held-out composites (baseline) are a pure no-viable-code (0 programs parse) failure**: 120/120 generations never become a viable program under the most favorable decode (favorable256; book_prefix80 syntax 0.000), so the 0.000 is not 'parses but computes the wrong composition' — semantics are never reached. The same pipeline scores syntax 1.000/pass@1 1.000 on primitives and syntax 1.000/pass@1 0.667 on exposed composites, so the pipeline itself is sound. **Wording axis (control a)**: rewording MASTERED primitive programs with never-seen template families yields syntax 0.020 and pass@1 0.000 (299/300 no-viable-code) vs syntax 1.000/pass@1 1.000 for the native wording — novel wording alone ALSO collapses generation, so surface-OD is a real contributor and must be controlled for — see control (b). **Surface-matched control (b)**: the identical held-out composite programs under verbatim training frames score syntax 0.075, viable 0.067, pass@1 0.000 (112/120 no-viable-code, 8/120 wrong-program) vs the native-prompt baseline syntax 0.000/pass@1 0.000 — verbatim frames move syntax only 0.000 -> 0.075 and pass@1 stays 0.000: no rescue, so the wording FRAME is not the confound. **Length-matched control (c)**: the NEW composites (reference token length asserted inside the mastered-primitive range) score unseen-surface syntax 0.000/pass@1 0.000 (80/80 no-viable-code) and seen-frame syntax 0.000/pass@1 0.000 (80/80 no-viable-code) — length is NOT the confound: at primitive-matched length the unseen composite still fails to produce viable code. **Verdict**: the composition 0.000 IS a no-viable-code generation failure (120/120 never parse, 0/120 wrong-program — semantics are never reached), and it SURVIVES both matched controls: verbatim training frames (b) leave 112/120 no-viable-code with pass@1 0.000, and at primitive-matched program length the new composites are 80/80 + 80/80 no-viable-code under BOTH wordings (c) — so neither wording frame nor program length explains the 0.000. IMPORTANT qualification from control (a): rewording MASTERED primitive programs with never-seen families ALSO collapses generation (299/300 no-viable-code, syntax 0.020 vs 1.000 native), so no-viable-code is this model's generic response to out-of-distribution prompts, and unseen composite structure is one such trigger — sufficient even when the sentence frame is verbatim from training (prompt length is ruled out: the seen-surface exposed control runs at comparable prompt length with syntax 1.000). The book's structural-generalization conclusion therefore survives the matched controls as a GENERATION failure on unseen compositions (never a wrong-program/semantic failure), but its mechanism is prompt-OD generation collapse, not failed composition attempts: the honest claim is that the model cannot generate code for unseen compositions (nor for seen programs under unseen wording), not that it composes incorrectly.
